digest.component_or_area: ADR (Architecture Decision Record) number assignment and validation
propositions: ADR corpus contains 91 files with only 69 distinct numbers; 17 numbers are duplicated across 22 files, causing collision ambiguity and stale cross-references.

Pre-merge CI uniqueness checks are inherently racy; race-free enforcement requires per-number marker files (docs/adr/.numbers/NNNN) whose content is the ADR filename, causing add/add merge conflicts on collision.
22 duplicate-numbered ADRs are renumbered to 0070–0091 (ascending landing-date order), earliest-landed ADR keeps its original number per tiebreak rule.

Every slug-bearing cross-reference (adr/NNNN-slug) across docs/ and src/ that names a moved ADR is rewritten to its new 0070–0091 number, with resolution tier and ambiguity recorded in RENUMBERING.md.
CI gate scripts/check_adr_numbers.py validates bijection (91 files ↔ 91 markers), unique marker content, and referential integrity (no dangling adr/*-slug links), exiting non-zero on violation.

Generated docs/adr/README.md index grouped by workstream and docs/adr/RENUMBERING.md resolution table with per-reference tiers (slug-exact, topic-matched, ancestry, UNRESOLVED) establish authoritative renumbering artifact.
